artworks.title: Landscape with Duck Hunters
artworks.dimensions: sheet: 21.8 × 31.6 cm (8 9/16 × 12 7/16 in.) cut to platemark
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Jimmy and Jessica Younger
artworks.description: The artwork depicts a landscape with a woodland scene viewed from a slightly elevated position. The horizon is positioned about halfway up the image, with open fields and a few scattered trees stretching into the distance. The left side shows a dense cluster of trees with full canopies, while the right side features two figures, possibly hunters, with dogs among foliage. The brushstrokes are precise, with detailed crosshatching techniques used for textures. The color palette is monochromatic, using various shades of black and grey. In the distance, an open and expansive landscape is bordered by a cloudy sky.

artworks.title: Young Woman Seated in a Garden
artworks.creditLine: Purchased for the Virginia and Ira Jackson Collection
artworks.description: The image shows a woman seated on a bench. She has delicate facial features, with a prominent nose and a contemplative expression, gazing to her left. Her hair is styled in an elegant updo. She is wearing a dress with puffed sleeves and a fur collar. The background is lush with large leaves and blooming flowers. No jewelry or objects are visible in her hands.

artworks.title: Hoche, Joubert, and Ossian [Ossian Receiving the Shades of French Heroes]
artworks.artist: Hyacinthe-Louis-Victor-Jean-Baptiste Aubry-Lecomte, after Anne-Louis Girodet de Roussy-Trioson
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: The image shows a bearded man with a bald head and a long beard, facing to the right and holding a staff. He is dressed in a flowing garment secured with a brooch on his shoulder. Other figures are partially visible around him, some holding staffs. The background is softly shaded, creating a sense of depth with gradually blurring figures.

artworks.title: The Lamentation
artworks.artist: Frans van den Wyngaerde, after Sir Anthony van Dyck
artworks.medium: etching with engraving on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: The image features a group of individuals gathered around a central figure who is lying down. The person is reclined on a cloth, with long hair and a beard, appearing unclothed but partially covered. Other figures are present: one individual draped in loose fabric is touching the central figure's shoulder, while two winged figures, possibly cherubs, interact with the central figure and each other. One of the winged figures is a small child-like being reaching upwards. Another figure, possibly a female adult with long hair, is beside the winged individuals, reaching out with an open hand. The setting is outdoors under a large tree, with clouds in the sky and a wooden post in the background. Various objects, including a large circular platter and some tools, are visible in the foreground. The image is etched with detailed lines and shading.

artworks.title: Landscape with a Penitent Magdalene
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: The image shows an engraving of a natural scene with a rocky, wooded landscape including various trees and boulders. Foliage and rock formations obscure the horizon, creating an intimate outdoor setting. The engraving is detailed, with precise line work depicting textures of rocks, leaves, and bark. The color palette is monochromatic, using shades of grey to show depth and form. In the foreground, a woman stands next to a large rock with a cross near her, surrounded by nature. The landscape fades into shallow shadows in the background, emphasizing the complexity of the trees and rocky terrain.

artworks.title: View of the Moon
artworks.dimensions:
image (each): 5.8 cm (2 5/16 in.) diameter
overall: 8.2 × 17.3 cm (3 1/4 × 6 13/16 in.)
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mary and Dan Solomon
artworks.description: This is a photograph of two images of the moon. The left and right images feature the full moon, displaying its detailed craters and surface features in shades of gray and white. The photographs are set against a deep red background with gold text. The text credits the lunar photographs to Warren De La Rue and notes that they were enlarged and published by Smith, Beck & Beck in London. The template suggests that these images were meant for stereoscopic viewing.

artworks.title: "View of the Moon"
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mary and Dan Solomon
artworks.description: This is a photograph of two views of the Moon. The photograph presents two side-by-side images of the Moon, showcasing its cratered surface and distinct phases. The images reveal details of the lunar surface, like craters and shaded regions creating texture and revealing the Moon's rugged terrain. The photographs are printed on a card with a yellow border, featuring text indicating that the original negatives are by L. M. Rutherfurd and published by P. F. Weil in New York. The card itself titled "View of the Moon."

artworks.title: "Full Moon"
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mary and Dan Solomon
artworks.description: This image presents a stereoscopic view of the full moon, captured in two identical photographs placed side by side. The point of view is directed towards the moon, displaying its surface in detail with prominent craters and dark and light areas. The horizon is not applicable in this context as the image focuses solely on the lunar body. The photographs do not appear to involve brushstrokes, as this is more likely a photographic print showing the monochrome details of the moon's surface. The overall color palette is simple, dominated by shades of black, white, and grey, creating a stark and high-contrast effect against the deep black background of space, which is bordered by a wide, vibrant blue frame.

artworks.title: "The Moon"
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mary and Dan Solomon
artworks.description: This is a photograph of two lunar images in a stereoscopic format. The image features a pair of identical full moons against a black background, placed side by side. The surface of each moon shows visible craters and dark patches. The stereoscopic presentation involves two slightly offset images for a three-dimensional effect. The photograph is framed with a sepia tone, giving it an antique appearance, and has a thin yellow border around the outer edges.

artworks.title: "Full Moon"
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mary and Dan Solomon
artworks.description: This is a photograph of two identical black-and-white depictions of the full moon side by side, set against a dark background. The moons are detailed, capturing craters and surface textures, and the image is bordered by a vibrant orange frame. Text is present on the frame, including the publication number "No. 466" and the title "Full Moon." There is also a mention of "John P. Soule" along with an address "199 Washington Street, Boston."

artworks.title: "Full Moon"
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mary and Dan Solomon
artworks.description: This is a stereoscopic card featuring two identical images of the full moon, showcasing its craters and surface texture in detail. The card is on a beige background with inscriptions mentioning the photographer, Prof. H. Draper, and the publisher, C. Bierstadt, in Niagara Falls, N.Y. It notes that the negatives were taken with a silvered glass telescope, capturing the selenographic features of the moon.

artworks.title: Photographie Lunaire-- Region Centrale
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mary and Dan Solomon
artworks.description: This is a photograph of the Moon's surface. The image shows a detailed view of the Moon's central region, as indicated by the craters and varying surface textures. The photograph was captured with a direct magnification of 15 times, providing visibility of numerous craters of different sizes spread across the lunar landscape. The lighting casts shadows that enhance the visual depth and detail of the lunar topography. The photograph includes details such as the date "28 Mars 1890," the observatory involved "Observatoire de Paris," and the work of "M.Mrs Henry." There is also information about the age of the Moon, suggesting it was 192 hours old when the photograph was taken. The photographic print is mounted on a card that includes these annotations.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Woman from Lisieux, Argentelle
artworks.creditLine: Pepita Milmore Memorial Fund
artworks.description: The image shows a person sitting on a low surface. They are in a slightly turned seated position, facing towards the left side of the image, with their chin resting on their right hand. Their facial features appear soft, with visible dark eyebrows and eyes. The person is wearing a large, tall headdress with a cone shape, and has dark hair peeking from underneath. They are clothed in a long, layered garment that includes a cloak and a long skirt reaching the ground. Beside them, a wicker basket with a handle rests on the floor. The background of the image is a simple textured backdrop.

artworks.title: William V of Orange
artworks.artist: Isaac Lodewijk de la Fargue van Nieuwland
artworks.medium: watercolor over etching with pen and ink and gray and brown ink wash on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Anonymous Gift
artworks.description: The image shows two men and a horse. One man is on horseback, while the other is standing beside the horse. The man on horseback is visible from head to toe, seated upright. He wears a tricorn hat decorated with a black and white feather trim, a blue coat with gold buttons, tan breeches, and black riding boots. He holds the reins of the horse in one hand and a sword in the other. The horse is light brown with a white mane and tail. The second man, standing beside the horse, has white hair partially covered by a golden and black-trimmed helmet. He wears a red coat with gold embroidery, tan stockings, and gold shoes. The background includes greenery, trees, a clear sky, and a white tent in the far background.

artworks.title: Frederica Sophia Wilhelmine
artworks.artist: Isaac Lodewijk de la Fargue van Nieuwland
artworks.medium: watercolor over etching with pen and ink and gray and brown ink wash
artworks.creditLine: Anonymous Gift
artworks.description: The image shows a person seated sideways on a dappled grey horse. The person is turned slightly towards the viewer, with delicate facial features including rosy cheeks and slightly pursed lips. They have short, curled hair beneath an ornate hat adorned with feathers and possibly flowers. They are wearing an elaborate blue coat with white and gold embroidery, a pink undergarment, light-colored gloves, a sash, and hold the horse’s reins. In the background, there is lush greenery, a tall tree, and a second person on horseback with a crown, set against a blue sky with soft white clouds.

artworks.title: Tourelle, Rue de la Tixeranderie
artworks.medium: etching in brown on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: The image displays a detailed and ornate building facade from a slightly elevated point of view. The perspective focuses closely on architectural elements, including tall chimneys and a pointed turret reaching toward the sky. The etching technique emphasizes intricate lines and cross-hatching to depict texture on bricks, stones, and foliage. The color palette is monochrome, using shades of brown to create an aged and historical look. In the foreground, there are figures and trees, adding depth to the scene, with additional details extending toward distant architecture in the background.

artworks.title: Venus and Bacchus
artworks.artist: Netherlandish 16th Century (formerly attributed to Cornelis Cort)
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: This is a drawing of mythological figures and symbols. The image shows a group of figures in an elaborate procession or dance. The figures are muscular and scantily clad, some with horns and holding objects like a trident. The central figure holds a staff and could be wearing a crown of leaves. The figures are surrounded by elements like vessels, a cornucopia, and decorative details. The drawing displays meticulous detail and cross-hatching in the shading.

artworks.title: Buzz Aldrin Poses with Flag
artworks.artist: Neil Armstrong, National Aeronautics and Space Administration
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mary and Dan Solomon
artworks.description: This is a photograph of the moon's surface featuring a U.S. flag and a person in a white spacesuit. The dark sky beyond contrasts with the brightly lit surface of the gray moon, which is covered in fine, grey dust featuring numerous footprints. In the center of the photograph, the flag stands on a thin rod and extends outward to the left. The person in the spacesuit is on the right, facing the flag. On the left side of the image, parts of a metal object are visible, which look like a metallic framework.

artworks.title: Maria Stuard condotta al patibolo (Mary Stuart Being Led to the Scaffold)
artworks.medium: lithograph on chine collé on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a crowded medieval court scene. It features a large group of finely dressed individuals in an elaborate interior space with high ceilings, arched windows, and sculpted figures. At the center, there is an elevated platform with steps, where a figure stands prominently, while armored guards are positioned at the stairway. The attendees are in varied poses and expressions, suggesting a sense of anticipation or solemnity. The atmosphere conveys a sense of historical significance and social hierarchy, enhanced by detailed attire and regal setting.

artworks.title: Study for "Dogma of the Redemption: Frieze of Angels" [verso]
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist)
artworks.description: The image depicts a full-body sketch of a person standing upright. The individual is holding a tall ladder in both hands, with their arms bent at the elbows. The facial features are simple and somewhat expressionless, framed by short hair or possibly a simple head covering. The clothing appears to be a long, draped garment that covers the body from head to foot, with layered fabric that folds around the figure. No jewelry is visible, and no additional objects are held by the person other than the ladder. The background is plain, with no distinct features. The paper has a somewhat aged appearance, with visible signs of tape at the edges and discoloration.

artworks.title: Bénigne-Charles Févret de Saint-Mémin
artworks.artist: Charles B. J. Févret de Saint-Mémin
artworks.medium: mezzotint and engraving in black on wove paper mounted to brown wove paper
artworks.dimensions:
image (irregular): 5.24 × 5.08 cm (2 1/16 × 2 in.)
sheet (trimmed to plate): 6.83 × 6.35 cm (2 11/16 × 2 1/2 in.)
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran)
artworks.description: The image depicts a profile portrait of a man with distinguished facial features. He is facing to the right, with his hair styled back and tied with a ribbon. The man is wearing a formal coat with a high collar and a shirt with a ruffled ascot or cravat. There are no visible signs of jewelry or objects in his hands. The background is simple and shaded, with a textured surface. At the bottom, there is handwritten text that appears to be a signature or attribution, along with a name in decorative script.

artworks.title: Charles de Lagarenne
artworks.artist: Charles B. J. Févret de Saint-Mémin
artworks.medium: mezzotint and engraving in black on wove paper mounted to brown wove paper
artworks.dimensions:
image (irregular): 5.56 × 5.56 cm (2 3/16 × 2 3/16 in.)
sheet (trimmed to plate): 6.83 × 6.35 cm (2 11/16 × 2 1/2 in.)
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran)
artworks.description: This is a portrait of a man in profile. He has a prominent nose and strong chin, with short wavy hair. He is wearing a high-collared coat and a cravat around his neck. The background is simple and circular. The image is in an antique, monochromatic style.

artworks.title: Robert R. Livingston
artworks.artist: Charles B. J. Févret de Saint-Mémin
artworks.medium: mezzotint and engraving in black on wove paper mounted to brown wove paper
artworks.dimensions:
image (irregular): 5.56 × 5.56 cm (2 3/16 × 2 3/16 in.)
sheet (trimmed to plate): 6.83 × 6.35 cm (2 11/16 × 2 1/2 in.)
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran)
artworks.description: The image features a portrait of a man in profile facing to the right. The man has a sharp nose, defined facial features, formal wavy hair tied with a ribbon, and is dressed in period formalwear. The background is shaded in a circular shape, with the text "Chancellor Livingston Robert R." written on a darker band at the bottom. An artist's note credits Valnais for the drawing and St. Memin for the engraving in New York.

artworks.title: Madame Jean de Sèze
artworks.artist: Charles B. J. Févret de Saint-Mémin
artworks.medium: mezzotint and engraving in black on wove paper mounted to brown wove paper
artworks.dimensions:
image (irregular): 5.4 × 5.4 cm (2 1/8 × 2 1/8 in.)
sheet (trimmed to plate): 6.83 × 6.35 cm (2 11/16 × 2 1/2 in.)
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran)
artworks.description: The image shows a bust-length side profile portrait of a woman facing right. She has a straight nose, a faint smile, and curly hair styled in an elegant manner with a headband and a large bow. She is wearing a garment with a ruffled collar, a shawl, and a long, drop-shaped earring. The background has a dark circular frame around her with text and artist credits in the lighter surrounding area.
